tip: Let your voice go up on 'Hello!' and stress the first part of LI-ly /ˈlɪli/.
'Seven' has two syllables: SEV-en /ˈsevn/. Touch your top teeth to your bottom lip for /v/.
'This' and 'little' have a short /ɪ/. For 'cat' /æ/, open your mouth wide.
Join the words: 'like apples' sounds like 'li-kapples'. Stress ba-NA-nas.
Breathe out for the /h/ in 'has'. Don't drop it!

text: We live in a small house.
tip: 'We' starts with round lips /w/. 'live' ends with teeth on your lip /v/.
Put your tongue between your teeth for 'the' /ð/ and make it buzz.
'Three' has /θ/ (no buzz) and 'brothers' has /ð/ (buzz). Your tongue goes between your teeth for both!

text: My dog runs in the park.
tip: 'runs' ends with a buzzy /z/: /rʌnz/. In British English 'park' has a long /ɑː/ and no 'r' sound.

text: He gets up at seven o'clock.
tip: Link 'gets up at' so it sounds like 'get-sup-at'. Stress SEV-en and o'CLOCK.
Say 'can' softly as /kən/. Your voice goes up politely on 'please?'

text: The princess has long yellow hair.
tip: British English doesn't say the 'r' in 'hair' /heə/. Breathe out for the /h/.

text: There are four birds in the tree.
tip: 'tree' starts with /t/, not /θ/ ('three'). 'four' rhymes with 'door' /fɔː/.
Say 'don't' as one beat /dəʊnt/. It's 'do' and 'not' joined together.
Wh- questions usually go DOWN at the end. 'favourite' often has two syllables: /ˈfeɪvrɪt/.

text: It is a big green frog.
tip: Don't add a vowel: say 'green' /ɡriːn/, not 'ge-reen', and 'frog' /frɒɡ/.

text: My mum makes cakes on Sundays.
tip: 'makes' and 'cakes' end with a hissing /s/. 'Sundays' ends with a buzzy /z/.

text: The fairy lives in the forest.
tip: Stress the first syllable of each long word: FAI-ry, FOR-est.
'school' has a long /uː/: /skuːl/. Stress FOOT-ball and AF-ter.

text: I can swim, but I can't fly.
tip: Weak 'can' is /kən/. Strong 'can't' is /kɑːnt/ with a long British /ɑː/. The difference matters!

text: Thank you for the birthday present.
tip: 'Thank' and 'birthday' both have /θ/: tongue between your teeth and push air out. Stress PRES-ent.
The 't' in 'castle' is silent: /ˈkɑːsl/.

text: My kite is red and yellow.
tip: 'kite' and 'my' share the same /aɪ/ sound. Open wide, then smile: /kaɪt/.
'bunny' has a short /ʌ/ like 'up'. Say BUN-ny and stress the first part.

text: I brush my teeth every night.
tip: Put your tongue between your teeth for 'teeth' /tiːθ/ and blow softly.
Let your voice jump up on RAIN-bow! Stress the first part.
Stress the first part: FRI-days, PIZ-za. The 'zz' in pizza sounds like /ts/.
'five' has /aɪ/ and ends with top teeth on your lip: /faɪv/.
Yes/no questions go UP at the end: 'with YOU?'
Round your lips for /kw/ in 'quack'. Say it like a happy duck!
Say 'blue' /bluː/ in one go, with no extra vowel: not 'be-lue'.
Stress MOR-ning. 'Miss' has a short /ɪ/ and a hissing /s/.

text: The cake is in the oven.
tip: 'oven' starts with /ʌ/ like 'up': /ˈʌvn/. Not 'oh-ven'!

text: Six snakes sleep in the sun.
tip: Make a long hissing /s/ like a snake. Go slowly first, then faster.

text: My shoes are under the bed.
tip: 'shoes' starts with /ʃ/ (shh!) and ends with a buzzy /z/: /ʃuːz/.
'It's' is 'it is' squeezed into one beat: /ɪts/. 'lunch' ends with /tʃ/.
Wh- questions usually go DOWN at the end. Stress OLD.
'eats', 'green' and 'leaves' all have a long /iː/. Smile wide!
'count' has /aʊ/ like 'ouch!'. Open your mouth, then round your lips.
'close' (shut) ends with a buzzy /z/: /kləʊz/. 'please' ends with /z/ too.
